Warm Milk Punch

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 10 min

Warm Milk Punch is a traditional festive drink often served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. This comforting beverage combines warm milk with spices, sugar, and a splash of brandy or rum, symbolizing warmth and celebration during the winter holiday.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups whole milk (960 ml)
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar (100 g)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/2 cup brandy or dark rum (120 ml)
  • Optional: whipped cream for topping
  • Optional: grated nutmeg for garnish

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine the milk, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
  2. Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it is hot but not boiling, about 8 minutes.
  3. Remove the saucepan from heat and stir in the vanilla extract and brandy or rum.
  4. Ladle the warm milk punch into mugs or heatproof glasses.
  5. If desired, top each serving with a dollop of whipped cream and a light sprinkle of grated nutmeg.
  6. Serve immediately while warm.

Tips

  • Use whole milk for a richer, creamier texture; you can substitute with half-and-half for extra richness.
  • Adjust the amount of brandy or rum to taste, or omit for a non-alcoholic version.
  • For a smoother texture, strain the punch before serving to remove any spice sediment.
